subject: Re: NovaHealth – clarifying output ownership / training consent (MSA + Order Form)
body:
From: contracts@novahealth.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: sara.chen@novahealth.com, legalops@novahealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Request: Output ownership & training consent language (MSA + Order Form)

Hi Markus,

Thanks for taking this through — attaching our redline of the MSA and order form. A few specific asks from our side that we want to resolve before procurement signs:

- Output ownership: we need explicit confirmation that NovaHealth will hold exclusive ownership of outputs (generated clinical care summaries) created by our prompts.
- Training / model retrain: we require opt-out by default for any use of NovaHealth data or outputs for model training, plus a mechanism to request swipe-level deletion of feedback artifacts.
- Feedback license: we are open to a limited feedback license for operational telemetry, but we want a narrowly scoped clause that excludes patient data and any PHI-derived artifacts.
- Attribution / downstream productization: we need a carveout preventing Redwood from using NovaHealth outputs in any product or training dataset that would be redistributed to other customers.

We attached our redline: NovaHealth_MSA_redline_20251129.pdf (see sections 3.2, 7.1, Exhibit B). Can you confirm which of these items Redwood can accept as-is, which require compromise language, and propose a short mutual action plan + timeline? We are on a compressed procurement window and would like legal alignment and an exec-level signoff by 12/6 if possible.

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a call today if helpful.

Regards,
Sara Chen
Head of Procurement, NovaHealth
contracts@novahealth.com
Attachment: NovaHealth_MSA_redline_20251129.pdf (PDF, 14 pages)

---

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: contracts@novahealth.com
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 11:05:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Request: Output ownership & training consent language (MSA + Order Form)

Sara —

Thanks for the detailed redline and context. Quick responses and next steps below. I’m copying Priyom (AE) for cadence and Laura (legal) for substance.

1) Output ownership: We generally grant customers broad rights to use and own outputs they generate, but there are two typical internal guardrails we discuss: (A) we ask for a limited, non-exclusive license back to Redwood for aggregated telemetry and quality monitoring (non-identifiable), or (B) a stricter model where customer outputs are fully excluded from any telemetry/training.

2) Training / retrain opt-out: We can offer a default opt-out for training on customer data/outputs (customer-managed telemetry opt-outs). We’ll need to define the scope and the operational mechanism (API flag + retention window).

3) Feedback license: We can narrow the feedback license to exclude PHI and provide explicit language that excludes patient-level data from any feedback dataset.

4) Attribution/downstream productization: We can accept a contractual carveout preventing Redwood from productizing NovaHealth outputs or including them in a commercial training dataset shared externally, but we’ll ask for an exception permitting use for internal safety/regression testing only, on de-identified/aggregated data.

Attachment: markus_response_redline.docx (our suggested clause alternatives inline).

Proposed mutual action plan:
- Today: Redwood to return proposed redlines on sections 3.2 (Outputs), 7.1 (Feedback/Telemetry), Exhibit B (Order Form definitions).
- Wed 12/3: Legal sync call (30 mins) between Laura + NovaHealth legal to finalize language.
- Fri 12/5: Final MSA/Order Form to procurement for signatures.

If this timeline is tough, flag and we’ll escalate to make room.

Thanks — I’ll wait for Laura’s legal framing and Priyom will coordinate scheduling.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Enterprise, Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.ai
Attachment: markus_response_redline.docx (DOCX, 2 pages)

---

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai; contracts@novahealth.com; sara.chen@novahealth.com; legalops@novahealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 Nov 2025 13:20:00 -05:00
Subject: RE: Request: Output ownership & training consent language (MSA + Order Form)

Markus / Sara —

Thanks for the redline. A few points from Legal (high level) plus a suggested set of compromise clauses (attached as redline_suggested_clauses.pdf):

- Outputs: We can accept a customer ownership statement for outputs that are created solely from customer prompts and non-Redwood system prompts. Proposed language: Customer shall own Customer Outputs, provided that Customer Outputs do not contain Patient-Identifiable Data as defined in Exhibit A. We propose a narrow definition of Customer Outputs to avoid claims for derivative training artifacts.

- Training / Model Retraining: We propose two-tier options in Exhibit B: (1) Opt-out: Customer may elect to opt-out of Product Training in writing (no feedback used for model training); (2) Opt-in for narrow telemetry: If Customer does not opt-out, Redwood may use anonymized/aggregated telemetry for algorithmic improvements, expressly excluding Patient Data and any data identified as PHI. We will add an operational clause that requires a 30-day advance notice prior to any retraining event using customer-provided data, and an audit right limited to verifying de-identification.

- Feedback License: Strongly recommend explicit exclusion of PHI and any raw patient artifacts. Suggested phrasing: Customer grants Redwood a limited, worldwide, royalty-free license to use Feedback solely to improve Redwood Services, provided that Feedback does not include Patient-Identifiable Data.

- Downstream Productization: We can offer a contractual commitment that Customer Outputs will not be included in any commercial training dataset offered to third parties. Redwood requests a carve for internal safety/regression use only, and we will accept contractual constraints around retention and deletion on request.

Operational asks for NovaHealth:
- Confirm whether clinical summaries flagged as PHI are automatically excluded or whether you require an API-level flag when content contains PHI.
- Confirm the acceptable retention window for telemetry (suggested default 90 days for raw logs, 24 months for aggregated metrics).

Next steps (proposed):
- I’ll send a tracked redline with the three compromise options (attached).
- Prio call Wed 12/3 11am ET to finalize (please confirm availability).

If NovaHealth needs an exec escalation, we can have our GC loop in — but I think we can reach a pragmatic compromise at the legal sync.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Commercial
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Attachment: redline_suggested_clauses.pdf (PDF, 6 pages)
